This staging minimizes command-and-control connections to evade detection, and data may be kept separate or combined via archiving. 2578.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
2578.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion is MITRE ATT&CK technique T1497, used for Defense Evasion and Discovery on Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. It involves detecting analysis environments by checking for artifacts like security tools (e.g., Sysinternals), virtual machine hardware, or low user activity, and then altering malware behavior to disengage or delay execution with sleep timers to avoid sandbox analysis. Sub-techniques include System Checks (T1497.001) and User Activity Based Checks (T1497.002). It is associated with groups like DarkHotel and OilRig.[/profile]
2578.profile_without_enhance_5_without_retriv: [profile]Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion is a defense-evasion and discovery technique (platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS) where adversaries detect and evade virtualized environments or analysis sandboxes to avoid detection and analysis. This is achieved by checking for artifacts like specific processes, hardware, or registry keys associated with virtualization, and subsequently altering malicious behavior or halting execution to prevent security tools from observing the attack. Associated vulnerabilities include CVE-2021-1675, CVE-2025-53770, CVE-2025-20337, CVE-2023-20198, and CVE-2023-20273.[/profile]
2578.profile_without_enhance_5_without_profil: [profile]Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion, identified as MITRE ATT&CK technique T1497, is a defense-evasion and discovery tactic used across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. It involves malware detecting analysis environments by checking for artifacts like security monitoring tools (e.g., Sysinternals, Wireshark), virtual machine hardware or processes, and a lack of legitimate user activity (e.g., mouse movements, browser history). Upon detection, the malware may alter its behavior, disengage, or use sleep timers to evade temporary sandboxes. This technique is associated with groups like DarkHotel and Contagious Interview.

3217.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1187, known as Forced Authentication, is a Credential Access technique primarily targeting Windows platforms. It operates by tricking a system into automatically sending authentication credentials, such as NTLM hashes, to an adversary-controlled server. This is commonly achieved by embedding a resource link (e.g., a file:// or SMB path) in a malicious document or shortcut file (like .LNK or .SCF), which triggers an authentication attempt when opened. The technique can also exploit functions like EfsRpcOpenFileRaw to force SMB authentication via the MS-EFSRPC protocol. It is associated with vulnerabilities like CVE-2023-36584 and CVE-2023-38831 and has been used by groups including Dragonfly and DarkHydrus.[/profile]

It works by adversaries inserting malicious Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macros into base Office templates, such as Word's Normal.dotm or Excel's PERSONAL.XLSB, which execute code when the respective application starts. Adversaries bypass this by delivering payloads inside container files like .iso or .vhd; while the container itself bears the MOTW, the extracted internal files do not inherit this tag and can execute without security prompts. 8644.name:
rule M_Hunting_GOGETTER_SystemdConfiguration_1

{

     meta:

          author = "Mandiant"

          description = "Searching for Systemd Unit Configuration Files but with some known filenames observed with GOGETTER"

          disclaimer = "This rule is for hunting purposes only and has not been tested to run in a production environment."

 

     strings:

          $a1 = "[Install]" ascii fullword

          $a2 = "[Service]" ascii fullword

          $a3 = "[Unit]" ascii fullword

          $v1 = "Description=" ascii 

          $v2 = "ExecStart=" ascii 

          $v3 = "Restart=" ascii 

          $v4 = "RestartSec=" ascii 

          $v5 = "WantedBy=" ascii 

          $f1 = "fail2ban-settings" ascii fullword

          $f2 = "system-sockets" ascii fullword

          $f3 = "oratredb" ascii fullword

          $f4 = "cloud-online" ascii fullword

 

     condition:

          filesize < 1MB and (3 of ($a*)) and (3 of ($v*)) and (1 of ($f*))

}

8646.name:
rule M_Hunting_VBS_Batch_Launcher_Strings

{

     meta:

          author = "Mandiant"

          date = "2023-02-13"

          description = "Searching for VBS files used to launch a batch script."

          disclaimer = "This rule is for hunting purposes only and has not been tested to run in a production environment."

 

     strings:

          $s1 = "CreateObject(\"WScript.Shell\")" ascii

          $s2 = "WshShell.Run chr(34) &" ascii

          $s3 = "& Chr(34), 0" ascii

          $s4 = "Set WshShell = Nothing" ascii

          $s5 = ".bat" ascii

    

     condition:

          filesize < 400 and 

          all of them

}
